f3_program: collection("video_game_sale.proceeds_by_friend", "money_amount", "video_game_sale", source("the total amount of money the three friends received together"))
observe(at("video_game_sale.friends.count", "sale"), 3, "count", source("three friends"))
member("video_game_sale.proceeds_by_friend", "ryan.video_game_sale.proceeds", source("Ryan, the first of the three friends, received $50 more than Jason from his sales"))
member("video_game_sale.proceeds_by_friend", "jason.video_game_sale.proceeds", source("Jason received 30% more money than Zachary from selling his video games"))
member("video_game_sale.proceeds_by_friend", "zachary.video_game_sale.proceeds", source("Jason received 30% more money than Zachary from selling his video games"))
offset("ryan.video_game_sale.proceeds", "jason.video_game_sale.proceeds", 50, "dollar", source("Ryan, the first of the three friends, received $50 more than Jason from his sales"))
percent_more("jason.video_game_sale.proceeds", "zachary.video_game_sale.proceeds", 30, source("Jason received 30% more money than Zachary from selling his video games"))
remove("zachary_video_game_sale", "zachary", at("zachary.video_games.count", "current"), 40, source("Zachary sold 40 games at $5 each"))
observe(at("zachary.video_game_sale.price_per_game", "sale"), 5, "dollar_per_game", source("$5 each"))

product_relation("zachary.video_game_sale.proceeds", event_field("zachary_video_game_sale", "quantity"), at("zachary.video_game_sale.price_per_game", "sale"), source("Zachary sold 40 games at $5 each"))
query("sum", "video_game_sale.proceeds_by_friend", "sale")
assumptions: Ryan, Jason, and Zachary are the three members whose sale proceeds comprise the requested total.
The $5-each rate applies to each of Zachary's sold games.

f3_program: observe(at("leigh_fox.company_tenure.year", "October 2008"), 2008, "year", source("Vice President of Finance at Cincinnati Bell Technology Solutions Inc. (CBTS) from October 2008 to December 2012"))
observe(at("leigh_fox.company_tenure.year", "February 24, 2020"), 2020, "year", source("as of February 24, 2020"))
query("difference", at("leigh_fox.company_tenure.year", "October 2008"), at("leigh_fox.company_tenure.year", "February 24, 2020"))
assumptions: Leigh Fox's company tenure begins with the October 2008 CBTS role and continues through the source's February 24, 2020 as-of date.
The requested duration is represented at year granularity using the explicit numeric year components.

f3_program: observe(at("gym.towels_laid_out.count", "every_day"), 300, "count", source("every day, there are 300 towels laid out for guest use"))
observe(at("gym.towels_per_guest.count", "visit"), 1, "towel_per_guest", source("Each guest is given 1 towel during their visit"))
observe(at("gym.operating_clock.hour", "10:00 a.m."), 10, "clock_hour", source("10:00 a.m."))
observe(at("gym.operating_clock.hour", "2:00 p.m."), 2, "clock_hour", source("2:00 p.m."))
collection("gym.guest_arrivals_by_hour", "hourly_guest_count", "gym", source("In the first hour, 50 guests enter the gym"))
member("gym.guest_arrivals_by_hour", "gym.guest_arrivals.first_hour.count", source("In the first hour, 50 guests enter the gym"))
member("gym.guest_arrivals_by_hour", "gym.guest_arrivals.second_hour.count", source("In the second hour, 20% more guests enter than during the first hour"))
member("gym.guest_arrivals_by_hour", "gym.guest_arrivals.third_hour.count", source("In the third hour, 25% more guests enter than in the second hour"))
member("gym.guest_arrivals_by_hour", "gym.guest_arrivals.fourth_hour.count", source("In the fourth hour, one third more guests enter than in the third hour"))
observe(at("gym.guest_arrivals.first_hour.count", "first_hour"), 50, "count", source("In the first hour, 50 guests enter the gym"))
percent_more(at("gym.guest_arrivals.second_hour.count", "second_hour"), at("gym.guest_arrivals.first_hour.count", "first_hour"), 20, source("20% more guests enter than during the first hour"))
percent_more(at("gym.guest_arrivals.third_hour.count", "third_hour"), at("gym.guest_arrivals.second_hour.count", "second_hour"), 25, source("25% more guests enter than in the second hour"))

sum_relation(at("gym.guest_arrivals.fourth_hour.count", "fourth_hour"), at("gym.guest_arrivals.third_hour.count", "third_hour"), fraction(at("gym.guest_arrivals.third_hour.count", "third_hour"), 1, 3), source("one third more guests enter than in the third hour"))
partition("gym.guest_arrivals_by_hour", "gym.guest_arrivals.day.count", source("In total"))
product_relation("gym.towels_to_wash.day.count", at("gym.towels_per_guest.count", "visit"), "gym.guest_arrivals.day.count", source("Each guest is given 1 towel during their visit"))
query("value", "gym.towels_to_wash.day.count")
assumptions: The four numbered hours cover the complete stated opening interval.
Every towel given to a guest is among the towels that need washing that evening.

f3_program: collection("edgars_fashion_store.customers_by_week", "weekly_customer_count", "edgars_fashion_store", source("The store sells to 35 customers in the first week, twice as many in the second week, and triple as many as the first week in the third week"))
member("edgars_fashion_store.customers_by_week", "edgars_fashion_store.customers.first_week.count", source("35 customers in the first week"))
member("edgars_fashion_store.customers_by_week", "edgars_fashion_store.customers.second_week.count", source("twice as many in the second week"))
member("edgars_fashion_store.customers_by_week", "edgars_fashion_store.customers.third_week.count", source("triple as many as the first week in the third week"))
observe(at("edgars_fashion_store.customers.first_week.count", "first_week"), 35, "count", source("35 customers in the first week"))
multiple(at("edgars_fashion_store.customers.second_week.count", "second_week"), at("edgars_fashion_store.customers.first_week.count", "first_week"), 2, source("twice as many in the second week"))

multiple(at("edgars_fashion_store.customers.third_week.count", "third_week"), at("edgars_fashion_store.customers.first_week.count", "first_week"), 3, source("triple as many as the first week in the third week"))

partition("edgars_fashion_store.customers_by_week", "edgars_fashion_store.customers.three_weeks.count", source("The store sells to 35 customers in the first week, twice as many in the second week, and triple as many as the first week in the third week"))
observe(at("julio.commission_per_customer", "three_weeks"), 1, "dollar_per_customer", source("a $1 commission for every customer that buys in Edgars Fashion Store"))

product_relation("julio.commission.three_weeks", at("julio.commission_per_customer", "three_weeks"), "edgars_fashion_store.customers.three_weeks.count", source("a $1 commission for every customer that buys in Edgars Fashion Store"))
observe(at("julio.earning_period.duration", "three_weeks"), 3, "week", source("for the 3 weeks"))
observe(at("julio.salary.amount", "three_weeks"), 500, "dollar", source("a salary of $500 for the 3 weeks"))
observe(at("julio.bonus.amount", "three_weeks"), 50, "dollar", source("a bonus of $50"))
collection("julio.three_week_earnings", "earning_component", "julio", source("how much in total does he earn for the 3 weeks"))
member("julio.three_week_earnings", "julio.commission.three_weeks", source("Julio receives a $1 commission for every customer that buys in Edgars Fashion Store"))
member("julio.three_week_earnings", "julio.salary.amount", source("a salary of $500 for the 3 weeks"))
member("julio.three_week_earnings", "julio.bonus.amount", source("a bonus of $50"))
query("sum", "julio.three_week_earnings", "three_weeks")
assumptions: The commission rule applies to every customer across all three listed weeks.
The stated salary and bonus are earning components for the same three-week period.

f3_program: collection("colton.dolphin_stickers", "sticker", "colton", source("Colton had 72 dolphin stickers"))
observe(at("colton.dolphin_stickers.count", "initial"), 72, "count", source("Colton had 72 dolphin stickers"))
collection("colton.first_friend_group", "friend", "colton.social_circle", source("3 friends"))
observe(at("colton.first_friend_group.count", "gift"), 3, "count", source("3 friends"))
observe(at("colton.dolphin_stickers.per_friend_count", "gift"), 4, "sticker_per_friend", source("4 stickers each"))

product_relation("colton.gift_to_first_friend_group.quantity", at("colton.dolphin_stickers.per_friend_count", "gift"), at("colton.first_friend_group.count", "gift"), source("He gave 4 stickers each to 3 friends"))

transfer("gift_to_first_friend_group", "colton", at("colton.dolphin_stickers.count", "current"), "colton.first_friend_group", "colton.gift_to_first_friend_group.quantity", source("He gave 4 stickers each to 3 friends"))
offset("colton.gift_to_mandy.quantity", event_field("gift_to_first_friend_group", "quantity"), 2, "count", source("He also gave his friend Mandy 2 more than he gave his three friends total"))

transfer("gift_to_mandy", "colton", at("colton.dolphin_stickers.count", "current"), "mandy", "colton.gift_to_mandy.quantity", source("He also gave his friend Mandy 2 more than he gave his three friends total"))
offset("colton.gift_to_justin.quantity", event_field("gift_to_mandy", "quantity"), -10, "count", source("he gave Justin 10 less than Mandy"))
transfer("gift_to_justin", "colton", at("colton.dolphin_stickers.count", "current"), "justin", "colton.gift_to_justin.quantity", source("he gave Justin 10 less than Mandy"))
query("remaining_count", "colton.dolphin_stickers", "current")
assumptions: Mandy and Justin are additional recipients beyond the initial group of three friends.
